promo-xc-late.title: Free shipping is the slow one #shorts
promo-xc-late.description:
Here's the Christmas card order most people place. Design done on 25 November, into the cart, free economy shipping.

Canva's folded cards page lists economy as free, 11–20 days — with 1–2 business days of production on top. Count business days: Thanksgiving is a holiday, weekends don't count. The cards land in the middle of December or later, and you still have to write and post them.

The post office's own last date for First-Class Mail to arrive by Christmas is 17 December. That is the line.

promo-xc-dates.title: The date to order your Christmas cards by #shorts
promo-xc-dates.description:
Give yourself a week to write the cards, so they need to be in your hands by Friday 11 December. Count back:

Free economy shipping — order by Tuesday 10 November.
Standard — by Friday 20 November.
Express — by Wednesday 2 December.

Those are our sums from Canva's own numbers. Order before 5 pm, because Canva says a later order can add a day — and the delivery date at checkout is the one that counts.

promo-xc-uk.description:

And whatever the calendar says, Canva's help page says the most accurate delivery date is the one shown at checkout. Look at it before you pay.

promo-xc-bleed.title: Two lines every printed card needs #shorts
promo-xc-bleed.description:
Before you order printed cards from Canva, turn on the guides: File → Rulers and guides → Show margins, then File → Settings → Show print bleed.

Canva's help page: keep text and logos inside the margin; extend backgrounds to the bleed, not text. The bleed is 0.125 in (3.175 mm) on every side, and Canva says it cannot be adjusted.

Photo out to the bleed. Words inside the margin.
